title: Monitoring as code with Datadog
scenario: "The client standardises on Datadog. Monitors and SLOs must be code-reviewed like everything else." — Client platform owner
mission: Enable the Datadog Agent through GitOps, get APM with unified service tagging, and create monitors and an SLO with Terraform.
objectives: Protect the API key with workload identity / CSI

prerequisites.notes: Datadog trial account; DD_API_KEY and DD_APP_KEY in the environment (never in Git).

criteria.text: APM service customer-portal-api has env and version tags
Monitors and the SLO exist in Terraform state

expectedResult: Two observability stacks, both as code.
recovery: Agents crash: the secret is missing — re-run the secret script.
dont: Do not commit the API key
Do not create monitors in the UI

interview.question: Azure Monitor vs Datadog: how would you advise a client?

debrief: Unified tagging links traces, logs and metrics per env/version; monitors as code bring review and history. Advise on cost, team skills and multi-cloud needs.

checker.plan: Read-only: kubectl get pods -n datadog, terraform state list (70-datadog), Datadog API read.

validation.notes: Checker not implemented yet; needs a Datadog account.
